QF.id: AIF Valuation Taxation and Good Practices_31

question.text: Under CRS, financial institutions including AIFs (where applicable) are required to:

answer.text: Collect and report financial account information that jurisdictions automatically exchange with other jurisdictions
Conduct common reporting on stock trades

explanation.text: The Logic: The Common Reporting Standard (CRS), to which India is a signatory, requires financial institutions and AIFs, where applicable, to collect and report financial account information. The information is then automatically exchanged between participating jurisdictions to combat cross-border tax evasion (NISM XIX-A, p. 266). The Trap: The other options confuse CRS with domestic-only reporting, credit-rating activity, or stock-trade reporting. CRS is specifically about cross-jurisdictional automatic exchange of financial account information. Note: CRS is implemented in India through the Income-tax Rules and applies to reportable accounts held by tax residents of other participating jurisdictions.
